title: How Hawkins and Parker took over his dates
summary: He suggested Hawkins and Parker and then found their names as leaders; he had to fight for the leader's fee.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Q You made a nice record with J.C. Higginbotham-- do you remember much about that at all? Yeah well see, I procured... I got them a lot of musicians that were idle and could use a gig. Like Coleman Hawkins wasn't doin' nothin'. And I suggested him, I said "I think I could get Coleman Hawkins" 'cause he and I good friends and as soon as I asked Hawk, he said "yeah, man-- for a session, yeah." But like I said it wound up at a later date, it was his session and not mine. But he had the stronger name, naturally. But they didn't even let me-- they didn't consult me or let me know anything-- they did the same thing with Charlie Parker. Before I knew anything it was Charlie Parker's date and I was a sideman. But they wound up sendin' me the royalties, but the recognition I never got, and they didn't switch it back. That seemed kind of rude--there's a better word for it, but I mean, you know, to do that to someone that suggested them in the front

that they didn't want, and all of a sudden... they don't consult me... I had to fight for the leadership fee, through I think it was Fox -- what's that company that gets your money back for you -- Fox. Some kind of Fox, I think it's Fox. Well, they help you get your royalties, you know, back. And it was finally switched around that I could, you know. They didn't even offer me that. They could say, 'well we would like to use this guy's name, put it here cause it sells more records, but you still get your fee' you know. Which would have been all right. It was already in there cause they did it... So they did that twice that I could remember... and I was never consulted...
